Applied form ai-chdha’ ‘bring’. An intransitive motion verb: the entailed goal is obligatorily expressed as a locative (dir ya’), may be a person's location, and does not count towards transitivity.
Applied form bh1i-chdha’ ‘make pass through’. An intransitive motion verb; the entailed location does not count towards transitivity.
Applied form bhai’-chdha’ ‘forcefeed’. A verb of ingestion: the subject is not maximally distinct from the object.
Applied form ii-chdha’ ‘make drink’. A verb of ingestion: the subject is not maximally distinct from the object.
Applied form kai-dha’ ‘make hear’. A verb of perception: the subject is not maximally distinct from the object.
Applied form namki-chdha’ ‘join’. A lexical middle: the subject is not maximally distinct from the object.
Applied form o’ñxi-dha’ ‘hide (animate object)’. A lexical middle: the subject is not maximally distinct from the object. Requires the middle prefix jum-, (338).
Applied form saab-tuda’ ‘make fast (as punishment)’. A lexical middle: the subject is not maximally distinct from the object.
Applied form t1iñxi-dha’ ‘show’. A verb of perception: the subject is not maximally distinct from the object.
Applied form tulhiiñ-chuda’ ‘make suffer’. A lexical middle: the subject is not maximally distinct from the object.
Applied form ga’lhi-dha’ ‘sell to someone’. The buyer is entailed ((326), (327)) but cannot be expressed in the base clause (324b); the applied form promotes it to primary object.
Applied form abialh-dha’ ‘sell to someone on credit’. Borrowed from Spanish fiar; patterns with ga’ra’.
Applied form sopki-dha’ ‘tell someone a story’. The hearer cannot be an object of the base (331b) and is promoted by the applicative (332b).
Applied form iatgi-dha’ ‘lie to someone’. The frustrative t1i requires a potential hearer (336a), so the hearer is entailed; the perfective applied form is truncated (337).
Applied form 1xchoi-dha’ ‘hide something from someone’. A prototypical transitive (animate agent, inanimate patient): the person the patient is hidden from is promoted, (341).

Applied form jotxi-dha’ ‘send (to a person)’. The base entails a goal expressed as a locative phrase; the applied form entails an animate goal, (357b) versus (356b), and rejects a place-name DP (362).
Applied form bui-dha’∼iabui-dha’ ‘throw to someone.sg/pl’. The base has a goal and no recipient (363a), (364); the applied form's goal is an animate intended recipient (365).
Applied form baabui-dha’ ‘take away from someone (under something)’. The promoted source must be animate (369); the possession implicature runs from the promoted object to the subject.
Applied form nui’ñ-dha’ ‘shove at someone’. The promoted target is animate but there is no possession entailment: t1i cancels the contact, (373).

Applied form ba’k-chuda’ ‘build houses for someone’. No object prefix on the base ((296b), (307)), but the incorporated noun ba’ak ‘house’ is a syntactic argument (308).
